title: Finitely presented Zariski main finite factorization
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a separated, quasi-finite morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] [pqf-def-quasifinite], with $S$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Assume $f$ is of finite presentation, meaning locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Then there exist a scheme $T$, a quasi-compact open immersion $j:X\hookrightarrow T$ [def-weil-open-immersion], and a finite morphism $p:T\to S$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] of finite presentation such that $f=p\circ j$. The scheme $T$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

source.place: Tag 0F2N, label lemma-quasi-finite-separated-pass-through-finite-addendum; includes the factorization of the preceding lemma-quasi-finite-separated-pass-through-finite, with qcqs finite factor over qcqs S

proof.text: By [pqf-def-quasifinite], every singleton {f.asFiber x} is open. Use the canonical homeomorphism of [def-pc-scheme-fibre] to transfer this to openness of singletons in the set-theoretic fibre. For a point (x, hx) of the fibre over s, substitute s = f(x). Mathlib locallyQuasiFinite_iff_isDiscrete_preimage_singleton, applicable because local finite presentation implies local finite type [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], then gives LocallyQuasiFinite f. The Lean proof writes this predicate-conversion argument explicitly.

Apply the existing source-library theorem Scheme.Hom.exists_isOpenImmersion_isFinite_locallyOfFinitePresentation in WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.QuasiFiniteFactorization (Stacks 0F2N). Its hypotheses are exactly the supplied local quasi-finiteness, local finite presentation, separatedness, quasi-compactness and qcqs base. It supplies T, j, p with j a quasi-compact open immersion, p finite and locally of finite presentation, and j followed by p equal to f. This reuses an already proved theorem, including its finite-presentation refinement; it does not assume the current theorem or introduce a new obligation.

A finite morphism is affine [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], hence quasi-compact and separated, in particular quasi-separated, by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](2) to p over the qcqs base S to obtain CompactSpace T and QuasiSeparatedSpace T. Return these together with all witnesses and properties from the source theorem. No unit statement or realized proof step is bypassed.
